For pricing and scheduling purposes, the Contractor must anticipate exactly one (1) deployment day and one (1) redeployment day. If the operational window expands past 2 days due to delays, contractor can bill for standby days if this occurs. 2. How many forklift service days? Table 2 shows ﬁve separate one-day operations, while §1.5 lists much broader forklift periods. Response: Forklift service days are dependent on the equipment's arrival timeline and the subsequent movement of assets from Tarapoto Airport to the 5th BDE HQ. The ﬁve (5) separate one-day operations referenced in Table 2 establish the designated aircraft execution window. This 5-day window is intentionally structured to accommodate Air Force aircraft availability, scheduling ﬂuidities, and potential arrival delays into Peru. As stated in the Critical Notice, the Contractor must account for simultaneous forklift operations at both the airport and the HQ during these operational days. 3. How many vehicles/equipment items must be AGWASHed? The documents give two washers and four days but no workload quantity. Response: The Contractor will not be required to wash any rolling stock or vehicles under this contract. The precise workload quantity

and potential arrival delays into Peru. As stated in the Critical Notice, the Contractor must account for simultaneous forklift operations at both the airport and the HQ during these operational days. 3. How many vehicles/equipment items must be AGWASHed? The documents give two washers and four days but no workload quantity. Response: The Contractor will not be required to wash any rolling stock or vehicles under this contract. The precise workload quantity requiring AGWASH is estimated to be six (6) 463L pallets and three (3) QUADCON containers. 4. Clarify the backup response standard. The solicitation technical submission language references a 2-hour response / 4-hour repair / 6-hour replacement, while the PWS repeatedly requires backup/replacement within four hours. Response: To eliminate ambiguity, the Government requires a standardized 4-hour response time for all troubleshooting, repairs, or asset replacements. This 4-hour window represents the maximum allowable time from initial notiﬁcation of a mechanical or operational failure to the arrival of fully functional replacement assets or successful repair completion. This standard is mandatory to meet the rigid download and delivery schedule. 5. Please conﬁrm whether the Contractor is required to maintain cargo insuranc

a quantity of one (1) forklift. The Government’s requirement is outcome-based. The contractor shall provide sufficient forklift support to safely and efficiently offload equipment from the aircraft at Tarapoto Airport, load it onto transportation assets, and subsequently offload the equipment at 5th BDE HQ within the required performance timeline. Whether this is accomplished with one (1), two (2), or more forklifts is at the contractor’s discretion. The solicitation CLIN quantity of one (1) forklift reﬂects the minimum identiﬁed requirement and does not prescribe the contractor’s method of performance. 2. The response to Question 6 references transportation to a “ﬁnal destination in Sauce. ” Please conﬁrm whether this was intended. The PWS and Technical Exhibit identify the required line-haul route as approximately 5.1 km between Tarapoto Airport and 5th BDE HQ. The reference to a “ﬁnal destination in Sauce” in Response to Question 6 was not intended for this requirement. The required line-haul route for this effort is between Tarapoto Airport and 5th BDE HQ, as identiﬁed in the PWS and Technical Exhibit, a distance of approximately 5.1 kilometers. The wells were sampled in the order from least to most contaminated. A decontaminated positive displacement submersible mini-monsoon pump and disposable tubing were initially used to purge and collect the groundwater monitoring well samples and the sample parameters were allowed to stabilize prior to sampling . Since wells purged dry and there were pump mechanical issues, a disposable bailer was used on select wells once wells recovered to 80% pre-purge volume. When samples were being collected, the pump was initially placed to be within 1 foot of the water surface or the bailer was slowly placed into the well casing . Samples were collected by removing the inflow hose from the flow -through cell into the laboratory-provided sample containers directly from the tube or bailer; first hydrochloric-acid preserved containers for VOC analysis, then unpreserved containers for PAH analysis, and finally hydrochloric acid- preserved containers for DRO analysis. Purge water was collected in five-gallon buckets. The Low Flow Sampling Data Logs are provided in Appendix B. 4.0 FIELD ACTIVITIES The 2025

Leica VT1200S Vibrating Blade Microtome, BRAND NAME ONLY BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: The Jesse Brown VAMC, Research Dept is requesting this product called “Leica Brand name only - VT1200 S Vibrating Blade Microtomes” This procurement is required for research on diabetes mellitus for use in studies of the liver. The Leica VT1200 S Fully automated vibrating blade microtome and will be used to generate precision-cut liver slices (PCLS) for human and mouse liver tissue samples as an ex-vivo model of the liver. Liver slices can be experimentally manipulated to assess metabolic flux, gene expression, and protein expression. REQUIREMENTS AND SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS TO MEET OUR NEEDS: The Leica VT1200S Vibrating Blade Microtome is a fully automated instrument designed for high‑precision sectioning of fresh or fixed biological specimens. It features fixed 85 Hz vibration frequency, adjustable amplitude (0–3 mm), and adjustable sectioning speed (0.01–1.5 mm/s) to ensure consistent, high‑quality cuts. Its innovative blade‑holder design minimizes vertical deflection to below 1 µm, significantly reducing tissue damage and preserving specimen viability. The system supports multiple blade types, enables automatic feeding and retraction, and provides stored user profiles for multi‑us

high‑quality cuts. Its innovative blade‑holder design minimizes vertical deflection to below 1 µm, significantly reducing tissue damage and preserving specimen viability. The system supports multiple blade types, enables automatic feeding and retraction, and provides stored user profiles for multi‑user laboratory environments. Magnetic specimen holders, integrated buffer/ice bath options, and motorized vertical feed further enhance accuracy, ease of use, and reproducibility. These capabilities make the Leica VT1200S uniquely suited for demanding neuroscience, pathology, and research applications requiring precision sectioning. 2. The Contractor shall provide a dedicated or on-call fixed-wing air ambulance capability to transport U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) personnel and their dependents from Kwajalein Atoll, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) to a receiving medical facility in Oahu, Hawaii. 1.3 BACKGROUND The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (POH) maintains a field office on Kwajalein Atoll. Medical facilities on the island are limited to a basic clinic/ER capable only of patient stabilization. There is no capability for complex surgery, critical care, or long-term hospitalization on-island. In the event of a life-threatening or limb-threatening emergency, personnel must be evacuated to a higher level of care in Oahu, Hawaii (approx. 2,100 nautical miles). Delays of any kind increase the risk of severe injury or death. 1.4 OBJECTIVES □ Readiness: Maintain 24/7/3

As used in this clause— "Computer database" or "database" means a collection of recorded information in a form capable of, and for the purpose of, being stored in, processed, and operated on by a computer. The term does not include computer software. "Computer software"— (1) Means (i) Computer programs that comprise a series of instructions, rules, routines, or statements, regardless of the media in which recorded, that allow or cause a computer to perform a specific operation or series of operations; and (ii) Recorded information comprising source code listings, design details, algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulas, and related material that would enable the computer program to be produced, created, or compiled. (2) Does not include computer databases or computer software documentation. "Computer software documentation" means owner's manuals, user's manuals, installation instructions, operating instructions, and other similar items, regardless of storage medium, that explain the capabilities of the computer software or provide instructions for using the software. "Data" means recorded information, regardless of form or the media on which it may be recorded. The term includes

des technical data and computer software. The term does not include information incidental to contract administration, such as financial, administrative, cost or pricing, or management information. "Form, fit, and function data" means data relating to items, components, or processes that are sufficient to enable physical and functional interchangeability, and data identifying source, size, configuration, mating and attachment characteristics, functional characteristics, and performance requirements. For computer software it means data identifying source, functional characteristics, and performance requirements but specifically excludes the source code, algorithms, processes, formulas, and flow charts of the software. "Limited rights" means the rights of the Government in limited rights data as set forth in the Limited Rights Notice of paragraph (g)(3) if included in this clause. "Limited rights data" means data, other than computer software, that embody trade secrets or are commercial or financial and confidential or privileged, to the extent that such data pertain to items, components, or processes developed at private expense, including minor modifications. turnover_financial.text: reasonable. The Contracting Officer is responsible for the determination of price reasonableness. The proposal will be evaluated in IAW RFO FAR 15.404, Cost and/or price analysis. In terms of “price reasonableness” the Government will focus on whether the price is too high to be considered fair and reasonable. In terms of “cost realism”, the Government will focus on whether the cost is too low and not realistic for the work to be performed. The Government’s concern is that the offeror may not understand the requirement or may be offering such a low proposed cost price that there may be disruption to the program such as high employee turnover, or an inability to recruit and retain quality individuals. Cost realism is the process of independently reviewing and evaluating specific elements of the Offeror’s proposed cost elements to determine the following: whether the estimated proposed cost elements are realistic for the work to be performed; whether the proposed cost elements reflect a clear understanding of the requirements; and whether the proposed cost elements are consistent with the unique methods of performance described in the Technical Proposal.
